findings.statement: Collapsing positive relative depth to one undifferentiated P label is Q-V inexact on every declared carrier.
Frontier plus positive-depth parity is exact on 5x3-k3, 6x3-k3, and 6x3-k4, but fails as a whole-component identity on 4x4-k4 and 4x5-k4 with 20 and 335 mixed scalar classes respectively.
Under the frozen coarsest-first ladder, exact frontier-relative depth remains the selected common whole-component coordinate for ROLE_CAPPAR_REL_INC_ZOE across all five declared carriers.

Earlier sufficiency of positive-depth parity for interaction descriptors does not imply sufficiency after direct whole-component aggregation under ZOE. Exact depth magnitude can be redundant for an interaction coordinate yet load-bearing for component identity.

nonclaims: This does not prove exact relative depth is globally minimal; only the frozen frontier-only and RPAR compressions are rejected as common replacements.
RPAR remains a valid exact whole-identity recoding on the three carriers where its partition matches the exact ROLE_CAPPAR class count.
The result does not alter the OOO matched-dependency factorization already established in the exact-depth coordinate.
EW-RS-059 PRIMARY 3x6-k4 and BACKUP 5x3-k4 remain sealed.
No Q-A/Q-F, standard-7x6, universal theorem, or center-opening proof follows.
next_question: With exact relative depth retained, what mechanically generated descriptor-motif or DTS/circuit functionals on the OOO dependency-residue quotient span the scalar image without outcome-selecting individual triples?
